summary: Pricing tier misapplied during DST switch causing invoice line-rate discrepancy
description:
Issue summary: Customer reports that several invoice lines for March 1-2 were billed at the lower 'off-peak' rate even though their calls occurred during the standard peak window. The discrepancy appears to align with the DST transition (US) and affected multiple hourly billing buckets. Customer noticed a $1,420 difference on their monthly statement.

High-level timeline: TempestAI noticed the delta on 2026-03-02 after exporting hourly usage via the console. They opened a support chat which was escalated to billing. We accepted this ticket to triage and coordinate with metering and scheduler teams.
impact: Customer-facing invoice mismatch for dedicated account. Amount: ~$1,420. Risk of charge dispute and delayed payment. Affects finance reconciliation and internal reserved capacity accounting for TempestAI. No service degradation reported, only billing rate application discrepancy.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) In TempestAI prod-us-east, run hourly usage export for 2026-03-01 00:00 to 2026-03-02 23:59 (UTC) using Console > Billing > Usage CSV.
2) Compare per-hour rate column against rate table for customer (reserved dedicated tier A).
3) Observe hours 02:00-04:00 local (which overlapped DST boundary) labeled as 'off-peak' and charged at Tier B rate instead of Tier A.
4) Cross-check meter postback times in logs and scheduler rounding for hourly buckets.
observed_behavior: Several hourly buckets that fall into the customer's configured peak hours were billed at the lower off-peak rate. Metering postbacks timestamped correctly but were assigned to the wrong pricing buckets after scheduler bucketization that runs at the hour boundary.
expected_behavior: All usage within customer's configured peak window should be billed at reserved Tier A rates regardless of DST transitions. Hourly bucketization should account for DST shifts and the customer's timezone setting.
logs: 2026-03-01T02:00:03Z bucketizer assigned bucket=2026-03-01T02:00:00Z timezone=America/New_York effective_tz_offset=-05:00 computed_bucket_label=off-peak
investigation_notes: 2026-03-10 10:12 - Initial triage: billing observed mismatch in console export vs expected rate table. Assigned to Ben Gomez.
2026-03-10 11:05 - Billing confirmed invoice line IDs provided by customer. Temporary CSV attached in internal thread. Action: check scheduler bucketizer code paths around DST boundary handling.

2026-03-10 13:40 - Metering team: postbacks arrived with correct UTC timestamps. No duplication. Suspect bucketizer uses naive localtime conversion for locations in 'America/New_York' during DST transition.

2026-03-11 09:22 - Reproduced in staging by simulating postbacks across DST boundary. Confirmed bucketizer shifted one-hour window into off-peak because it used fixed offset mapping rather than tz-aware conversion.
comments: 2026-03-10 10:30 - Asha Patel (Support): Thank you for the report, TempestAI. We're opening a billing investigation and will update within 24 hours. Can you confirm whether your org timezone is set to America/New_York in Console > Settings?
2026-03-10 10:52 - TempestAI (customer): Confirmed. Org timezone: America/New_York. We saw the anomaly for 02:00-03:00 on 2026-03-01 local time.

2026-03-10 12:00 - Ben Gomez (Billing): We've pulled the invoice lines and initial suspicion is bucketization around DST. Looping in metering and scheduler. Assigning to INT-4042 for code investigation.

2026-03-11 09:30 - Metering Engineer (Priya Ramesh): Reproduced in staging. The bucketizer was using time.Local with a hardcoded offset in the hourly-roll function. Proposed patch: use tz-aware IANA conversions on the timestamp before computing bucket start.

2026-03-11 16:05 - Asha Patel (Support): TempestAI, thanks for your patience. We're proceeding with a credit for the impacted invoice line and will issue a corrected invoice after the code fix is deployed. ETA for patch: 2026-03-12 morning deploy to staging, 2026-03-12 evening deploy to prod.
2026-03-12 09:00 - TempestAI (customer): Appreciate the quick turnaround. Please confirm credit amount before posting.
resolution: Workaround: Manually adjust invoice lines for INV-2026-03-01-TEMP-001 for hours flagged in investigation (posted as provisional credit).
Fix: Scheduler/bucketizer patch merged (billing PR #2217) to use tz-aware IANA conversion and DST-aware bucket rounding. Patch deployed to prod on 2026-03-12 20:15 UTC.
Credit: Issued credit of $1,420.00 on 2026-03-12 applied to TempestAI account balance. Corrected invoice reissued as INV-2026-03-01-TEMP-001-REV1.
Verification: Post-deploy smoke check completed for 24h of simulated DST boundary traffic; no misapplied rates observed.
follow_up_tasks: INT-4042: Add unit/integration tests for bucketizer around DST transitions (assigned to Priya Ramesh).
Billing: Add a nightly audit that flags any hourly buckets where applied_rate != expected_rate based on customer's configured tier (owner: Ben Gomez).
Docs: Update billing runbook to include DST considerations and verification steps (owner: Finance Ops).
